exercise.name: Lever Kneeling Twist

reference.title: Lever Kneeling Twist
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment (gymvisual.com refused the request), so the data sheet was not read and the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)

equipment: Rotary torso lever (handles on an arm turning about a vertical axle, knee pad)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you twist, breathe in as you return.
breathing.cadence: About 1.3 s across, short hold, about 2 s back

prescription.effort: Stop 1-3 reps short of failure (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Load is user-chosen: light; twist smoothly through the ribs, hips square.

cues.text: Kneel tall on the pad with the hips square and the arms in front at chest height, both hands on the handles.
Breathe out and turn the chest and shoulders to the right, arms staying in front of the chest.
Hold the turn with the hips still facing forward.
Breathe in and turn back to the centre under control.
Pause facing forward; switch sides after the set.

mistakes.mistake: Turning the hips with the chest
mistakes.fix: Keep the hips square; rotate through the ribs.
Turn smoothly and stop before the end of range.
Keep the arms still in front of the chest.
Kneel tall with the chest up.

kinematics.norm: From facing forward to about 35-45 degrees of upper-trunk rotation (clinical opinion)
Hips square and still on the knee pad (clinical opinion)
Held in front of the chest; they turn with the trunk (clinical opinion)
The handles turn about a vertical axle lined up with the spine (clinical opinion)
Torso-twist exercise on a training machine activated the obliques well (Scientifica 2015 torso-twist study)
Controlled rotation under modest load; avoid jerky end-range twisting (McGill 1998)
About 1.3 s across and 2 s back (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #934, Lever Kneeling Twist, video (movement reference)
Torso-twist exercise with elastic resistance vs a training machine: core muscle EMG (Scientifica 2015:403068; PubMed 26557405)
McGill 1998, low back exercises: evidence for improving exercise regimens (Phys Ther 78(7):754-765; PMID 9672547)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Load is user-chosen: start light; rotation under load can irritate the low back.
Stop short of the end of your rotation range.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Low back discomfort: reduce the range and the load.
progressions: Pause 2 s at the turned position.

muscleNotes.obliques_r: Prime movers: rotate the trunk (external oblique of one side with the internal oblique of the other).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Prime movers: rotate the trunk (external oblique of one side with the internal oblique of the other).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Keep the trunk tall; the deep rotators help turn.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Keep the trunk tall; the deep rotators help turn.
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Hold the hips square on the pad.
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Hold the hips square on the pad.
